Subject: FinOps playbook sync & actionables — token economics and batching options

Thanks again for your time today, Alex and Sana — good conversation. Quick recap and the suggested next steps so we keep momentum: 

What we heard (pain + goal)
- Production latency spikes on peak transaction windows (affects fraud scoring & customer-facing chat).
- Token spend is the single biggest runway risk for this feature; current TCO modeling shows token > infra for your highest-volume flows.
- Goal: deploy a phased pilot that demonstrates 40–60% per-token spend reduction while keeping quality within current SLA for fraud classification and short chat responses.

Key levers we discussed
- Batching: grouping low-latency, high-frequency classification calls into short-window batches for GPU utilization (expected 20–35% token-cost reduction in our baseline sim).
- Prefix/KV caching: persistent cache for repeated customer context & templates (saves tokens on repeated prompts).
- Model quantization and a smaller candidate model for lower-cost routing during non-peak windows.
- Smart routing: route to cheaper variant when confidence threshold met; fallback to higher-quality model for edge cases.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) You (Ledgerly): send one week of anonymized token/profile distribution for the fraud classifier and chat sample traces we can use for a more precise pilot estimate (recommended CSV columns in the attached spreadsheet).
2) We (Redwood): produce a focused FinOps playbook + a 90-day pilot plan with projected unit economics, the expected token savings by lever, and measurable quality gates (we attached the initial playbook draft).
3) Align on decision criteria and procurement timeline so we can scope Dedicated or a Hosted trial accordingly.

Pilot acceptance criteria (proposal)
- >=40% reduction in per-request token spend or equivalent $/month reduction given Ledgerly projected volumes.
- No more than 2% delta in fraud-classifier precision at the chosen operating point.
- Operational readiness: basic observability (per-route token latency & cost).

Attachments referenced
- ledgerly_token-model.xlsx (token distribution template)
- FinOps_playbook_v1.pdf (initial playbook / pilot outline)

Proposed timing
- We can ingest anonymized traces early next week and return a pilot TCO synthesis within 4 business days.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a short calendar invite for a framing session to walk through the required CSV columns.

Hi Alex / Sana — appreciate the quick turnaround on traces. Short answers to your clarifications and what we’ll include in the pilot TCO: 

- Batching latency modeling: we simulate two batching modes in the pilot — micro-batches (10–50ms added queuing latency) and latency-bound batching that only groups prefetchable/async calls (near-zero added latency). For customer-facing sub-second flows we typically default to the latter and reserve micro-batching for backend scoring where 50–100ms is acceptable. We’ll surface per-flow latency vs. savings trade-offs in the report.

- KV caching with churn: even with higher churn we see substantial benefit for templated prompts and repeated metadata (customer tier, product flags). Typical lift is 8–18% token saving in churn-heavy streams once hot-key filters are applied. We’ll run the ledgerly traces through a caching sim and show per-route expected delta.

Pilot TCO deliverables we’ll provide after ingest: 
1) A per-route token-cost waterfall (current vs pilot) with modeled batch/caching/quantization savings.
2) Per-request latency heatmap and a recommended batching policy per route.
3) Suggested SLOs and quality gates for upgrade/fallthrough routing.
4) A one-page ROI summary for procurement (monthly $ delta at projected volumes).

We attached an initial FinOps playbook—read the appendix for CSV formatting (ledgerly_token-model.xlsx). If you want, Ben and I can join the ingest call to walk through the CSV and anonymization checklist.

Proposed next meeting: Thu, Apr 29 at 10:00am PT (30 min) to align the sample export and pilot timeline. I’ll send a calendar invite.
